reply.subject: RM_Muttavaq

observed.facings.png: Three facings on a checkerboard at one scale. All three show a broad, low slab of tan cracked clay with polygon plates radiating from a central point. Under the slab is a darker brown, folded hide body standing on four or five stubby, flared, organic legs. South and north are nearly the same width and height. East is a long oval profile with a tapered snout at the right end, under the rim.
observed.south.png: Front view. A thick, cracked-clay disc has about ten radial cracks meeting at a centre pit; its rim plates have rounded edges. Below the rim is a dark horizontal slit (the mouth or jaw-plate gap) across most of the width. Just under it, a loose row of about six small dark openings sits in the folded brown hide. Four squat, tapering legs with flared, mushroom-like feet. No eyes or face beyond the slit and openings. Clean white/alpha background, no shadow.
observed.east.png: Side profile. A long, flat cracked-clay carapace, more ellipse than disc, with radial cracks from an off-centre hub. A brown, wrinkled hide body runs underneath, with three visible legs that have flared feet. At the right end is a low, tapered, reptile-like snout under the rim with a long mouth seam and two small reddish openings or pits. It reads as a head pushed forward under the shell. No ground patch.
observed.north.png: Rear view. The same cracked-clay disc with radial cracks, and rim plates matching the south. Below is folded brown hide with vertical wrinkle folds and no slit, mouth or eyes. Four flared legs. Slightly more saturated orange than the south. No face.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom the creature is about 4 cells wide, far wider than the vanilla human (the human is about 1 cell tall), and its top is roughly at the human's head height. At 32 px/cell it reads as a flat tan cracked disc on short brown legs, clearly separate from the ground colour, beside a much smaller human and rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: The south shows the front: the dark mouth slit or jaw-plate gap under the rim, with sensory openings below it. It is a front-on view, not a profile or overhead.

NORTH_REAR.seen: The north shows only folded hide and legs under the rim: no slit, openings or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All facings use the angled 3/4 camera: the top surface is foreshortened and the rim side and legs are visible.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The measured height spread is 2%. South and north have matching widths in facings.png.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: The same radial-cracked clay carapace, brown folded hide and flared legs appear on every facing. The snout and mouth appear on east and south (as the slit) and are absent on north, as they should be.

SIGNATURE.seen: The carapace is a low, mounded polygon field with cracks radiating from a centre, which is exactly the 'cracks radiating from a center' clay pan. The jaw-plate mouth is visible on east and south.

ALIEN.seen: The silhouette is a turtle-like shelled walker, but the shell is a flat cracked clay pan and there is no tortoise head or neck. The mouth is a flat, slit-jawed snout under the rim, and the legs are hide-fold pillars. A stranger would see 'living cracked mud pan' before 'tortoise'.

STYLE.seen: The surface is painted, with plausible weathered clay and wrinkled hide. There are no glossy eyes or smile, and it is not cel-shaded. The finish is slightly smooth and CG-like but within range.

OURS.seen: A bespoke cracked-pan creature that matches no vanilla or known mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha on all three. No ground patch, shadow or halo is visible on the checkerboard.

OWNER_NOTES.seen: The north now matches the south in size (2% spread). The south face is a shadowed slit with irregular openings, not a cartoon face.

SCALE.seen: About 4+ cells wide beside a 1-cell human, consistent with 'canyon-floor giant' and drawSize 4.6.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a bold tan cracked disc on dark legs, clearly apart from the ground.

findings.seen: The sensory openings under the mouth slit are still small, roundish dark holes in a loose horizontal row of about six. They are less regular than before but can still read as a line of dot-eyes or buttons at a glance.
findings.quote: Glossy round eyes and a smiling face are cute.
findings.fix: The south sensory openings are a few uneven, slit-like or torn creases sunk into the hide folds at varied heights and sizes, merging into the shadow of the jaw-plates rather than forming a row.

findings.seen: South and north are nearly identical silhouettes. The only front cue is a thin dark slit under the rim, which disappears at 32 px/cell, so front and rear are hard to tell apart in normal play.
findings.quote: legibility at 32 px. Both are polish.
findings.fix: The south view shows the jaw-plates as a slightly protruding, darker lip under the rim's front edge, so the front reads as the mouth side even at 32 px.

findings.seen: The clay plates have a smooth, slightly rendered, uniform micro-texture and the legs are evenly modelled, which leans towards a 3D-render finish more than a painted vanilla sprite.
findings.quote: Not toy-figurine cel shading … not a photo or a 3D render.
findings.fix: The carapace and hide carry looser painted brushwork and a slightly firmer dark outline in the vanilla RimWorld manner.

proposals: Consider a subtle front cue on the south (protruding jaw-plate lip) so the south and north facings differ legibly at normal zoom.
A sleeping/dug-in lifestage or graphic (just the clay pan flush with the ground) would sell the 'reads as terrain' concept better than the walking sprite can.

reply.subject: RM_Muttavaq
reply.image_seen: The shared-scale panel and three individual facings show a broad, cracked ochre pan over a dark folded body with squat limbs; the scale panel shows it dwarfing a human and remaining recognizable at normal play size.

concerns.evidence: On south, the openings vary from narrow slits to an angular central cavity, with uneven spacing and different heights within the hide folds. They do not form paired eyes or a cute expression. East shows elongated openings beneath the projecting jaw rim. At normal play size these resolve into underside detail rather than dot-eyes.

The plates have angular mottling, but also broken pale edge strokes, irregular dark cracks and uneven ochre patches. The undersides and limbs show layered brown strokes with irregular contours and asymmetric folds. At the shared scale and normal play size, these read as painted clay and hide; the enlarged surface facets do not establish a blocking 3D-render finish.
